title: From spec to running MCP server

nodes.label: Next.js dashboard
nodes.note: App Router UI on Vercel: spec upload, tool editor, build progress, security findings, analytics, billing and team pages.

nodes.label: MCP client
nodes.note: Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client. Authenticates with a JWT or an mcpforge_live_ API key.

nodes.label: REST API
nodes.note: /api/v1 routers for specs, servers, tools, build, security, credentials, billing and team. Request-ID, CSRF, CORS and per-IP rate-limit middleware.

nodes.label: Auth services
nodes.note: JWT httpOnly cookies with token rotation, Argon2 passwords, HIBP check, Redis account lockout, GitHub OAuth, email verification and password reset.

nodes.label: Playground WebSocket
nodes.note: playground/ws.py. JSON-RPC over WebSocket to test draft or deployed tools, with in-memory sessions that are never persisted.

nodes.label: MCP gateway
nodes.note: gateway/mcp_server.py. /mcp/v1/{slug} over SSE or StreamableHTTP. Authenticates, loads server config, enforces plan rate limits.

nodes.label: Tool dispatcher
nodes.note: Decrypts the credential, builds the auth header and the HTTP request from stored tool config, runs the SSRF guard, retries, formats the MCP result.

nodes.label: AI description worker
nodes.note: ai queue. Rewrites each tool description with the LLM, scores it with a regex-based quality scorer, and publishes per-tool progress.

nodes.label: Security scanner
nodes.note: scanner queue. Eight rules in rules.py, such as DELETE without auth, credential fields in responses and prompt-injection text.

nodes.label: Analytics worker
nodes.note: analytics queue plus Celery beat: records tool calls, aggregates hourly, creates daily partitions, drops old ones weekly.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.note: Celery broker and result backend, pub/sub for SSE progress, Lua-script rate limits, server-config cache (5 min TTL), lockout counters, Stripe event dedupe.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.note: SQLAlchemy async models for users, servers (tools_config JSONB), credentials, versions, scans, API keys, teams and a day-partitioned tool_calls table.

nodes.label: S3 spec storage
nodes.note: Raw OpenAPI specs written through aioboto3, de-duplicated by SHA-256 hash.

nodes.label: LLM provider
nodes.note: OpenAI-compatible client with a configurable base URL, defaulting to a DeepSeek model, with retries and JSON mode.

nodes.label: GitHub OAuth
nodes.note: Optional sign-in. State values are stored server-side by oauth_state.py.

nodes.label: Resend email
nodes.note: Verification and password-reset emails over its HTTP API, falling back to log output when no key is set.

nodes.label: Stripe
nodes.note: Checkout, customer portal and subscription webhooks, signature-verified and deduplicated for 7 days in Redis.

nodes.label: Customer API
nodes.note: The REST API the MCP tools wrap. Reached over HTTPS only after the SSRF guard passes.

flow: A spec is uploaded or fetched by URL, validated, hashed, stored in S3 and analysed into tool definitions in Postgres.
Starting a build enqueues a Celery task on the ai queue through Redis and returns a job id immediately.
The worker rewrites each description with the LLM, scores it, saves it, and publishes progress through Redis pub/sub, which the API streams to the dashboard as SSE.
The security scanner runs its eight rules against the tool set on its own queue before the server goes live.
An MCP client connects to the gateway with a JWT or API key; the gateway checks plan rate limits and reads the server config from the Redis cache.
Each tool call becomes an HTTP request, passes the SSRF guard and goes to the customer's API.
Secondary path: the gateway fires a Celery event after every call, and the analytics worker writes it to a daily-partitioned table that beat aggregates hourly.
Secondary path: Stripe subscription webhooks hit the API, are signature-checked and deduplicated, then sync the user's plan.
